svg.title: Sequence the Platform, or Sequence the Outcome?
svg.desc: A decision tree with three questions. The first asks whether anything has yet reached a real consumer. If not, the recommended path is one bounded data product delivered end to end; the alternative, building the platform and its frameworks first, is flagged as the warning branch because it produces no outcome to validate against. The second question asks whether a second workload is genuinely required by a consumer or is being added speculatively. The third asks whether a domain needs its own capacity, which turns on whether its workloads are actually contending for compute rather than on org-chart boundaries.
svg.text: Sequence the outcome, then earn the platform
A decision guide for the next delivery increment, workload, and capacity boundary in Microsoft Fabric

g.text: A named person uses the output

g.aria-label: Has anything reached a real consumer yet?
g.title: Has anything reached a real consumer yet? — The root question. Everything else in the sequence depends on whether a real user is already being served.
g.text: Has anything reached a real consumer?
Name the person · the decision · evidence of repeated use

g.title: Deliver one bounded data product — One source, through OneLake, to one semantic model and one report that a named person actually uses.
Platform-first delivery with no outcome — Frameworks, medallion layers, and governance models built before anything is consumed.
g.text: COURSE CORRECT → CUT THE THIN SLICE

g.aria-label: Is a second workload actually required?
g.title: Is a second workload actually required? — Second question: is the new workload pulled in by a consumer, or pushed in speculatively?
g.text: Name the dated consumer requirement first.

svg.text: QUESTION 3 · DRAW COMPUTE BOUNDARIES FROM EVIDENCE

g.aria-label: Does a domain need its own capacity?
g.title: Does a domain need its own capacity? — Third question: separate capacity is a compute-contention and cost-boundary decision, not an org-chart one.
g.text: Do domains actually collide under load?
Use observed contention and chargeback needs — never the reporting hierarchy alone.
Contention or cost isolation is real

svg.text: Did another workload earn its place?
Every route above lands the same Delta Parquet — the thin slice is never a dead end for later engines
Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset; evidence keys in tooltips.
